title: Geometric Inquiry Theory
subtitle: Establishing geometric bases for inquiry through Q-State Dynamics and the structural basis of inquiry.
audience: Mathematicians, physicists, and theoreticians working on the geometric and formal foundations of inquiry and cognition.
lede: Geometric Inquiry Theory develops a geometric framework for understanding inquiry as a structured dynamic process — establishing Q-State Dynamics and the structural basis of inquiry as a coherent mathematical theory, drawing on a multi-decade background spanning paramedicine, network engineering, and culinary arts as informal laboratories.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The project establishes geometric and algebraic foundations for inquiry — treating the act of asking questions as a structured, consequence-laden process with formal properties. Q-State Dynamics provides the theoretical core, with protocols documenting the empirical and epistemological basis of the work.

It asks why exactly six interrogative operators — who, what, where, when, how, and why — recur across natural languages and cognitive systems, and whether this is a structural necessity rather than a linguistic accident, with relevance to how constraint structures emerge, persist, and fail in multi-agent AI alignment settings.

sections.heading: Participate
sections.body: Mathematicians, physicists, and formally-oriented theoreticians interested in the foundations of inquiry are welcome.
